$comment: Reviewed exceptions for scripts/test-translations.mjs, each with its reason. `numbers`: places where a zh/fa translation may carry different figures from the English source; `where` is the location the test prints ('*' matches anything). `tokens`: a brand or unit name that is identical in uz, ru and en (so the test treats it as an identifier) but has a standard native form in zh or fa; each entry allows exactly ONE `value` in ONE `locale` at ONE `path` (the location the test prints, no wildcards), and only while the source still reads `source`. Structure and placeholders can never be allowed here, and no other identifier.

numbers.reason: GLOSSARY §1.4b: on zh pages the form accepts any international number, so the hint shows +86 / +998 examples instead of the Uzbek-only '+998 XX XXX XX XX'.

GLOSSARY §1.4b: on fa pages the form accepts any international number, so the hint asks for the country code with Iranian and Afghan examples (+98 / +93) instead of the Uzbek-only '+998 XX XXX XX XX'.
GLOSSARY §1.4b: the zh form accepts any international number, so the error asks for the full number with its country code instead of '+998'.
GLOSSARY §1.4b: the fa form accepts any international number, so the error asks for the full number with its country code instead of '+998'.

DECISIONS.md §1: Persian dates are numeric and never use month names, so the English 'Customs rules from May 1' can only be written with its year: ۲۰۲۵/۰۵/۰۱, the year of the Spot.uz article it cites (date 2025-04-23).

tokens.reason: The messenger's standard Persian name (GLOSSARY §3: Telegram → تلگرام), the one every other fa string writes ('در تلگرام به ما پیام دهید'); the mobile bar was the last Latin 'Telegram' on fa pages.
A unit, not an identifier: Chinese writes the foot as 英尺, as the zh rail page title does (20 英尺和 40 英尺柜). Same figures.
A unit, not an identifier: Persian writes container sizes as ۲۰ فوت / ۴۰ فوت (Persian digits, the unit as a word, DECISIONS §1). Same figures.
The platforms' own Chinese names (GLOSSARY §3), the names Chinese readers know them by; the paragraph above the table already says 淘宝和拼多多.
The platform's own Chinese name (GLOSSARY §3), as the zh buying page title writes it (1688、淘宝、阿里巴巴代采购).
The platforms' own Chinese names (GLOSSARY §3); the same table row's note already says 天猫为官方店铺；淘宝看卖家评分和评价. The site name Alibaba.com in the row below stays Latin.
The platform's own Chinese name (GLOSSARY §3); the paragraph above the table already says 拼多多最便宜.
